subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Musical structure is an important part of composition.
• In sonata form, there is a section called the exposition.
• It is one of several sections in a musical piece.
prompt: The student wants to provide an example of a section in sonata form. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In musical composition, some sections are parts of a piece.
choices.B: The exposition is an example of a section in sonata form.
choices.C: Sonata form includes several sections in a musical piece.
choices.D: Musical structure is an important part of composition, including sonata form.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it directly accomplishes the stated goal of providing an example of a section in sonata form. The sentence explicitly names 'the exposition' and identifies it as 'an example of a section in sonata form,' using the specific information from the second note. This choice effectively synthesizes relevant information from the notes to fulfill the rhetorical purpose, giving readers a concrete instance of what a section in sonata form looks like rather than merely describing that such sections exist.
